## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `quota-bounded-retrieval-funnel`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-07T15:37:10.972Z.

(7) Two-stage retrieval funnel with per-source candidate quotas — (1)-(6) specify how to SCORE and PACK, but at millions of items (pm-g2zz) the scorer must never see the whole workspace; the missing explicit piece is the recall stage of the classic recall-then-rank architecture. Candidate generation unions bounded top-k slates from independent cheap sources, each with its own quota: (a) ANN top-k from the hybrid semantic index, (b) n-hop graph expansion from focus/claims/plan steps (the seed set of (2)), (c) top-k by folded activation from the write-time view of (6) (a simple sorted structure makes this O(k)), (d) the agent's own WIP/claimed set and watermark-delta (novelty candidates), (e) exact lexical/field-predicate hits. Per-source quotas guarantee slate DIVERSITY structurally (no single degenerate signal floods the pool) and make cost independent of workspace size: scoring is O(sum of quotas), never O(items). Quotas scale with the token budget, which is how the same funnel serves a 3-item scratch workspace (every source returns everything, union is the whole workspace) and a decades-deep archive unchanged — the spectrum invariant. Explainability extends naturally: --explain-ranking reports which source(s) recalled each candidate before the per-signal score breakdown. SDK-side behind scoreContextCandidates like (1)-(6); composes directly with (5) RRF, which can fuse the per-source ranks as its cold-start combiner.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
